chunks: With this chain of transmission, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Samāʿah, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a mouse that falls into the well, or a bird. He said: If you reach it before it becomes putrid, you should draw seven buckets from it. If it is a cat or something larger than it, you should draw thirty buckets or forty buckets from it. And if it has become putrid such that the smell of rottenness is found in the water, you should drain the well until the foul smell goes away from the water.

key_terms.الْبِئْرِ: the well whose water is being discussed for purification
key_terms.الْفَأْرَةِ: a mouse that has fallen into the well
key_terms.رِيحُ النَّتْنِ: the smell of putridity found in the water
key_terms.سَبْعَ دِلَاءٍ: seven buckets to be drawn as a purification measure
key_terms.نَزَحْتَ الْبِئْرَ: to drain or draw out water from the well
key_terms.يُنْتِنَ: to become putrid or produce a foul odor

ai.seo_question: What should be done if a mouse, bird, or cat falls into a well according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about purifying well water when an animal falls into it. It specifies different amounts of water to be drawn depending on the size of the animal and whether decomposition has affected the water's smell.
